_readme: Copy this file into your research folder as queries.json and edit it.
problems: one key per customer problem (snake_case). The list holds the search term in each language, in the same order as 'languages'. Use null to skip a language.
Write the words a customer would type or an ad would say, in everyday language, not the product category. Native-speaker wording beats a literal translation.
fb_country: which Meta Ad Library country to search for each language (Scrape Creators). ALL = no country filter.

trendtrack.min_days_by_language: use 60+ for big foreign markets (DE, FR, NL, Nordic countries) so you only get ads that have been running long enough to be profitable ('proven abroad'). Use 0 for your own markets so you also see new competitors.
Each source is switched on with on: true. run_queries.py prints the credit estimate and stops; it only spends credits with --go.

advertisers: fill these after the first digest, with the competitors you want to pull in full. TrendTrack ids come from 'trendtrack.py lookup <domain>' (free). Facebook page ids come from the Ad Library URL or from /v1/facebook/adLibrary/search/companies (1 credit).
All keys starting with _ are ignored.
name: posture-example

fb_adlibrary._pages_note: page 1 = up to 30 ads, page 2 = up to 10 more. The API caps a query at about 40 ads, so pages > 2 rarely adds anything.

social._note: TikTok / Instagram / YouTube search is NOT filtered by country. Search in the local language and filter results by region or author afterwards (digest.py social).
